evidence.quote: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce its reliance on products from Nvidia and Huawei
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei, per Reuters citing three unnamed sources.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (three unnamed sources)

evidence.quote: DeepSeek's chips are being designed specifically for inference
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek's chip project is reportedly designed for AI inference, per unnamed sources cited by Reuters.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (three unnamed sources)

evidence.quote: Nvidia's position in China is effectively at zero and will remain that way.
evidence.one_line: Analyst Richard Windsor of Radio Free Mobile says Nvidia's China position is effectively zero and will stay so.
evidence.speaker: Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile

evidence.quote: Huawei has expanded its domestic market share and now controls around half of China's AI chip market, which is valued at approximately US$50 billion.
evidence.one_line: Huawei reportedly controls around half of China's AI chip market, valued at about US$50 billion.
evidence.speaker: idnfinancials.com (citing Reuters)

evidence.quote: Reuters previously reported that the company was preparing its first funding round worth US$7 billion, with a valuation of between US$52 billion and US$59 billion
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek was reportedly preparing a first funding round of US$7 billion at a valuation of US$52-59 billion.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (unattributed sources)

evidence.quote: In April, DeepSeek launched its V4 model, which had been optimised for Huawei Ascend chips, while Huawei revealed that training for the V4-Flash model also used Ascend processors.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek launched V4 in April optimised for Huawei Ascend; Huawei said V4-Flash training also used Ascend processors.
evidence.speaker: DeepSeek and Huawei

evidence.quote: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, called Jalapeno, last month in collaboration with Broadcom
evidence.one_line: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, Jalapeno, in June 2026 with Broadcom.
evidence.speaker: OpenAI

evidence.quote: The base model supporting DeepSeek R1 was trained using Nvidia's H800 chips, a product specifically designed for the Chinese market before the US government banned its export in late 2023.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek R1's base model was trained on Nvidia H800 chips before the US banned H800 exports in late 2023.
evidence.speaker: US government and DeepSeek
